title: Revit Working Library - QA and Review

entries.name: Pre-issue view graphics check
checks: correct view template applied to intended issue views
temporary overrides removed or explicitly justified
line weights and patterns legible at target print scale
filled regions, masking regions and detail lines used only where appropriate
linked-model visibility controlled intentionally
levels, grids and section/elevation heads do not collide with content
hatch patterns and material graphics remain legible

entries.name: Sheet and view consistency check
checks: approved titleblock/configuration in use
required project information populated and current
sheet numbers and names are unique and governed
view names comply with the applicable naming rule
callouts and references resolve correctly
view placement is readable and consistently aligned
revision information matches the issue state
notes, legends and schedules use governed sources where available

entries.name: Annotation and spelling check
checks: approved or governed text/tag types used where available
manual text-format overrides minimized
spelling checked before issue
technical terms and abbreviations checked against the applicable glossary
leaders and arrowheads remain readable and consistent
units and notation render correctly in the issued output

entries.name: Model hygiene and issue-readiness check
checks: temporary worksets, imports and troubleshooting content reviewed
unused or stale links identified
duplicate or ad-hoc content identified for reconciliation
project information and required parameters present
export views and issue sheets use repeatable governed states
known unresolved items are recorded rather than silently ignored

working_rules: A QA check produces evidence; it does not itself grant formal acceptance, authorization or publication authority.
Checks should distinguish objective findings from professional or contractual judgment.
Missing governing values should produce an unresolved or indeterminate state rather than an invented pass criterion.
Representative print/export tests are useful evidence where style quality cannot be established from model metadata alone.

provenance.migration_note: Style-focused QA checks retained as non-authoritative working data. Role, organization, client and project identifiers removed; acceptance authority remains outside this library.
